subject.title: [Bug] Docker sandbox container name collision across multiple instances on same host

question: Should OpenClaw accept workspace-qualified non-shared sandbox runtime identity, including the documented one-time runtime reset, as the fix for this sandbox collision?
rationale: The source-proven bug needs a fix, but the active repair changes sandbox identity and upgrade behavior across security-sensitive runtime boundaries.

options.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
options.body: Land the current candidate after maintainer/security sign-off on the one-time non-shared runtime reset.

options.title: Require an upgrade migration
options.body: Add a doctor or migration path first if preserving old non-shared sandbox runtime state matters.

options.title: Split the backend policy
options.body: Pause the candidate fix if Docker, browser, SSH, and skills workspace identity should not move together.

recommendation.title: Accept workspace-scoped identity
recommendation.body: Land the current candidate after maintainer/security sign-off on the one-time non-shared runtime reset.

likelyOwner.reason: History shows the strongest current and prior ownership signal in the sandbox security/runtime path, and the related lifecycle issue is authored from this account.
